PC-GEN-018.explanation: Under California Insurance Code section 330, neglecting to communicate a fact a party knows and ought to communicate is concealment, and section 331 lets the injured party rescind whether the concealment was intentional or unintentional. Misrepresentation is an affirmative false statement rather than silence.

PC-POL-012.explanation: Required insurance is 80 percent of $500,000, or $400,000. Carried over required is $300,000 / $400,000 = 0.75, so the insurer pays 0.75 x $100,000 = $75,000.

PC-HO-015.explanation: Payment lasts for the shortest time needed to repair or replace the damage or for the household to settle elsewhere, limited by the Coverage D amount rather than a fixed number of days or the policy period. In California, a covered loss tied to a declared state of emergency gets at least 24 months of additional living expense, extendable to 36 months for delays beyond the insured's control (Insurance Code section 2060).

excluded.PC-AUTO-018: Key is 'varies by state'; California Insurance Code 11580.2(q) prohibits stacking UM limits, so the national answer is misleading for CA (replaced by PCCA-CAAUT-009).
excluded.PC-AUTO-030: ISO 60-day cancellation rule; California Ins. Code 1861.03(c) and 661 restrict auto cancellation and nonrenewal at all times, and the explanation defers to state rules.
excluded.PC-LIA-017: Asks for the X/Y/Z employers liability limits, which the house rules forbid.
excluded.PC-GEN-010: California Ins. Code 286 requires insurable interest in property both when the insurance takes effect and at the loss, so 'at the time of the loss' alone is misleading for CA.
excluded.PC-HO-016: Civil authority ALE capped at two weeks; Ins. Code 2060(c) gives at least two weeks plus two-week extensions for good cause in a declared emergency.
excluded.PC-AUTO-015: Explanation says UM property damage varies by state; California's UMPD rule was not verified for this form, so the item was left out.
